answer: Charge each account for the reserved capacity it can consume, including idle reservations. A market that runs glacier simulations, saffron yield models and sparrow surveys assigns every queued job a unique capacity lease. The scheduler debits the lease for each reserved GPU minute and refunds only unused time released before scheduling. Aliases cannot reserve the same minute twice or bypass the charge. To crowd out honest agents, a farm must buy as much compute time as it blocks, even if it never runs useful jobs.
